source_caption:
The famous charcoal sketch of Rose wearing the Heart of the Ocean wasn’t actually drawn by Leonardo DiCaprio, but by director James Cameron, who is an accomplished illustrator. The tight close-up shots of the charcoal hitting the paper are actually Cameron’s hands at work, not DiCaprio’s. However, because Cameron is left-handed and DiCaprio is right-handed, the post-production team had to horizontally mirror the footage of the drawing process so it would seamlessly match Jack’s handedness in the final cut. Cameron also chose to keep a genuine flub from DiCaprio during the scene—when Jack nervously tells Rose to lie “on the bed... the couch”—believing the actor’s real-life anxiety perfectly captured the character’s awe and intimidation in that intimate moment.

Titanic (1997), directed by James Cameron, starring Leonardo DiCaprio, Kate Winslet, Billy Zane. A wealthy teenage aristocrat and a struggling working-class artist fall passionately in love aboard the luxurious, ill-fated R.M.S. Titanic during its disastrous maiden voyage in 1912.

source_details.synopsis: Titanic is a 1997 American epic historical romance film written and directed by James Cameron. Incorporating both historical and fictional aspects, it is based on accounts of the sinking of RMS Titanic in 1912. Leonardo DiCaprio and Kate Winslet star as members of different social classes who fall in love during the ship's ill-fated maiden voyage. The ensemble cast includes Billy Zane, Kathy Bates, Frances Fisher, Bernard Hill, Jonathan Hyde, Danny Nucci, David Warner and Bill Paxton. Cameron's inspiration came from his fascination with shipwrecks. He felt a love story interspersed with human loss would be essential to convey the emotional impact of the disaster.
